architecture.goal: Refactor the phase-2 Step Functions workflow so it becomes the single owner of operational history, pending-record lifecycle, idempotency fail-fast behavior, retry policy, and final persistence, while the consumer Lambda becomes pure business execution.
runtime_shape: Producer Lambda reads eligible PENDING records and publishes one SQS FIFO message per work item
Orchestrator Lambda consumes one SQS message and starts one Step Functions execution with an enriched operational payload
The state machine performs operational orchestration through native DynamoDB integrations and one Lambda invoke task
Consumer Lambda only calls the provider API and returns business success or throws classified errors
The state machine persists final success or failure evidence in tapi-results and closes pending/idempotency state

module_boundaries.responsibility: Parse SQS payload, enrich workflow metadata such as TTL strings, and start one Step Functions execution per work item.
Own the operational story: idempotency, lifecycle transitions, retries, failure routing, and final persistence.
Execute the provider API call and return or throw business outcomes without persisting results.
Handle lock acquisition, pending lifecycle updates, idempotency completion/failure, and results persistence using Step Functions service integrations.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: WorkflowInput
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Canonical input shape for the state machine after orchestration enrichment.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: ConsumerInvokePayload
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Payload injected into the business Lambda.
interfaces_and_contracts.shape: Exactly the original work-item fields only. The Lambda does not require workflow metadata to perform the provider call.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: ConsumerSuccessResult
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Successful business response returned by the Lambda to the state machine.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: ConsumerFailureContract
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Error classification used by Step Functions retry and catch logic.

state_machine_definition.context_preservation_rule: The original workflow input must remain available after InvokeConsumerLambda. Lambda response data must be stored under a dedicated result node instead of replacing the root input.

states.name: AcquireIdempotencyLock
states.responsibility: Claim the logical work item before business execution.
states.result_handling: Discard service response and preserve original workflow input.

states.name: MarkPendingInProgress
states.responsibility: Advance the lifecycle from PENDING to IN_PROGRESS.
states.result_handling: Discard service response and preserve original workflow input.

result_handling.rule: Store the Lambda success payload under $.consumerResult and keep root workflow fields intact for downstream DynamoDB states.

states.name: PersistSuccessResult
states.result_handling: Discard service response and preserve workflow input.

states.name: MarkIdempotencyCompleted
states.responsibility: Close the idempotency record as COMPLETED.

states.name: MarkPendingCompleted
states.responsibility: Mark the pending record as COMPLETED.

states.name: PersistTerminalFailureResult
states.responsibility: Persist terminal failure evidence in tapi-results.
states.note: Implementation may normalize terminal error payload into a stable DynamoDB-friendly map before this state if Step Functions cannot project the thrown shape directly.

states.name: PersistExhaustedFailureResult
states.responsibility: Persist exhausted transient failure evidence in tapi-results.

states.name: MarkIdempotencyFailed
states.responsibility: Close the idempotency record as FAILED for terminal or exhausted paths.

states.name: MarkPendingFailed
states.responsibility: Mark the pending record as FAILED.

states.name: DuplicateWorkItem
states.responsibility: Finish duplicate or no-longer-claimable work as a no-op operational success.

states.name: WorkflowCompleted
states.responsibility: Terminate a successful or duplicate workflow.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Use native Step Functions DynamoDB integrations for lock acquisition, lifecycle transitions, and results persistence.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: This keeps Lambda compute focused on business execution and reduces cost.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Use a single LambdaInvoke task only for provider business execution.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: The consumer Lambda remains pure and the state machine owns operational persistence.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Keep WorkflowInput TTLs as string numerics.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: Native DynamoDB task integrations require numeric attribute values to be passed through numberFromString semantics.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Use full jitter in retry behavior for transient failures.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: This avoids herd effects against provider APIs while preserving retry resilience.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: Catch the conditional failure and finish in DuplicateWorkItem without invoking the consumer.
Catch the conditional failure in MarkPendingInProgress and finish in DuplicateWorkItem.
Persist success evidence and close lifecycle as COMPLETED.
Skip retry, persist terminal failure evidence, and close lifecycle as FAILED.
Retry with exponential backoff and full jitter until attempts are exhausted, then persist exhausted failure evidence and close as FAILED.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: Lambda response envelope overwrites workflow input
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: Forbidden by design. The invoke task must preserve the original root input and store Lambda output under a dedicated node.

quality_gates: Unit tests cover the consumer as pure business logic without results persistence.
State machine synth reflects native DynamoDB integrations and jitter-enabled retries.
Manual execution of the workflow proves success path, terminal failure path, exhausted transient path, and duplicate no-op path.
expected_test_scenarios: Manual execution with a valid pending record reaches PersistSuccessResult and MarkPendingCompleted on HTTP 200.
Manual execution with HTTP 400 reaches terminal failure path without retry.
Manual execution with HTTP 503 retries with backoff and full jitter, then reaches exhausted failure path if retries are consumed.
A duplicate or already-claimed record ends in DuplicateWorkItem without invoking the consumer.
The workflow input remains available after InvokeConsumerLambda for downstream DynamoDB states.

phased_implementation_plan.goal: Make Step Functions the single operational owner of phase-2 execution history.
tasks: Remove results persistence responsibility from the consumer Lambda.
Refactor LambdaInvoke to preserve original workflow input and store success output under a dedicated result node.
Add native DynamoDB success persistence state.
Split terminal and exhausted failure persistence into state-machine-owned branches.
Add retry configuration with BackoffRate 2.0 and JitterStrategy FULL.
Validate duplicate no-op behavior and success/failure lifecycle closure end to end.
definition_of_done: The consumer Lambda is pure business execution only.
The state machine owns final persistence to tapi-results.
Workflow input survives the consumer invoke step.
Terminal and exhausted failures close through explicit failure states.

assumptions: The consumer Lambda can be changed to return structured success payloads and throw classified errors without writing to DynamoDB.
Duplicate executions should not write rows into tapi-results.
A stable error normalization step may be needed if direct Step Functions access to thrown error shape is insufficient for results persistence.
